ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows the same geometric figure: the vertex Q of the large triangle PQR is above, the base PR is horizontal, point S is on the base PR, segment QS goes from Q perpendicular to the base, and there is a right-angle mark at S. The triangle on the left is △PQS, and the triangle on the right is △RQS. In the figure, PS is labeled x, SR is labeled 2y, the left slanted side PQ is labeled 2x, and the right slanted side RQ is labeled 3y+8. Reasoning: The problem gives △PQS ≅ △RQS, with the correspondence by vertex order being P ↔ R, Q ↔ Q, S ↔ S. Therefore corresponding sides are equal: PS = RS, so x = 2y; PQ = RQ, so 2x = 3y + 8. Substitute x = 2y into 2x = 3y + 8 to get 2(2y) = 3y + 8, that is, 4y = 3y + 8, so y = 8.
